title: Liver
source: OpenStax A&P 2e: 23.6 Accessory Organs in Digestion: The Liver, Pancreas, and Gallbladder

main.t: The largest gland in the body: it makes bile and processes the nutrients and toxins absorbed from the gut.

simpler.t: Your liver is a big organ under your right ribs. It makes bile and cleans your blood.

deeper.t: Besides digestion, it has many roles in metabolism and regulation.

facts.t: It lies below the diaphragm in the right upper quadrant of the abdomen, protected by the ribs.
Peritoneal folds called ligaments attach it to the diaphragm and the abdominal wall.

simpler.t: It sits high on the right side of your abdomen, under your ribs.

deeper.t: The lesser omentum tethers it to the lesser curvature of the stomach.

items.name: Right and left lobes
items.t: A large right lobe and a much smaller left lobe.

items.name: Quadrate and caudate lobes
items.t: Smaller lobes some anatomists identify within the right lobe.

items.name: Falciform ligament
items.t: A remnant of the umbilical vein that separates the right and left lobes in front.

items.name: Porta hepatis
items.t: The “gate” where the hepatic artery and hepatic portal vein enter.

simpler.t: Two main lobes, with vessels entering at a “gate” underneath.

deeper.t: It weighs about three pounds (about 1.4 kg) in an adult.

facts.t: Hepatocytes, about 80 percent of its volume, line porous sinusoids and process what the blood brings.
It makes about one litre of bile a day; bile salts emulsify fats.
Bile salts are reclaimed in the ileum and recycled (the enterohepatic circulation).

simpler.t: Its cells sit right against the blood, clean it, and make bile to break up fats.

items.name: Hepatic portal vein
items.t: The hepatic portal vein brings nutrient-rich blood from the gut. It supplies more oxygen than the hepatic artery.

items.name: Hepatic artery
items.t: Brings oxygenated blood from the heart.

items.name: Gallbladder
items.t: Stores and concentrates the bile between meals.

items.name: Common bile duct
items.t: Formed by the common hepatic and cystic ducts; carries bile to the duodenum.

simpler.t: Blood comes in from the gut and the heart; bile goes out to the gallbladder and duodenum.

facts.t: The falciform ligament and the ligamentum teres hepatis are remnants of the fetal umbilical vein.
Some anatomists divide the right lobe further into quadrate and caudate lobes.

items.injury: A blockage that stops bile reaching the intestine.
items.damaged: The flow of bile into the duodenum.
items.cannotDo: Digest fats normally: the stool is pale (acholic) and fatty.
items.why: Without bile, fats are not emulsified and bilirubin does not colour the stool.

items.injury: A build-up of bilirubin when red cell breakdown or bile flow goes wrong.
items.damaged: The liver’s excretion of bilirubin into bile.
items.cannotDo: Clear bilirubin: the skin and eyes turn yellow (jaundice).
items.why: Bilirubin is a waste of old red cells that the liver normally excretes in bile.
items.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–17, 19–23 and 25). Jaundice and its causes.

items.q: Explain how bile helps digest fats.
model: Fats do not dissolve in the watery chyme.
Bile salts have a water-loving and a fat-loving region.
They pull large fat globules apart into droplets about 1 micrometre across.
This emulsification gives lipase a larger surface to act on.

items.q: Compare the blood the liver receives from the hepatic artery and the hepatic portal vein.
model: The hepatic artery brings oxygenated blood from the heart.
The portal vein brings partly deoxygenated, nutrient-rich blood from the gut.
The portal vein also carries absorbed drugs and toxins.
It actually supplies more oxygen than the smaller hepatic arteries.

items.q: Predict what happens to bile between meals.
model: Bile is diverted into the gallbladder.
There it is concentrated and stored until the next meal.

options: Behind the stomach in the retroperitoneum
check.why: It lies inferior to the diaphragm in the right upper quadrant.

check.stem: What enters the liver at the porta hepatis?
options: Hepatic artery and hepatic portal vein
check.why: The hepatic artery and hepatic portal vein enter at the porta hepatis.

check.stem: What gives faeces their brown colour?
check.why: Intestinal bacteria turn bilirubin into stercobilin, a brown pigment.
